=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1144]] is assessed at 99% (proved). James’s will names Archibald among his sons, and the 1817 equity complaint independently places him among James and widow Mary’s children. The Newberry household, age and distinctive sibling group identify this Archibald.

Existing supported father99%; source transcriptions are held, originals not newly inspected. Archibald’s birthplace and Mary’s maiden surname are not established here.

Next useful test: Use the estate and cemetery family to test Archibald’s proposed later son Robert.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://www.lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_JGlasgowWill.html James Glasgow will, dated4 June 1775, proved 1793, Newberry Will BookA p194; retained derivative transcription]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://www.lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_Reply.html Newberry Glasgow family equity complaint and Robert’s sworn answer,2 June 1817; retained derivative transcriptions]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Original 1810 household — 30 October 2026 ===
The original 1810 Newberry schedule, page 119 A, names Archd Glasgow. In the five ordered age columns (under 10, 10–15, 16–25, 26–44, 45 and over), males read 2, blank, blank, 1, blank; females read 1, 1, 1, 1, blank. The other-free column is blank and the enslaved-person tally is 6. Only the head is named. No male aged 10–25 is tallied, so the unnamed 1800 boy cannot be tracked through this household in 1810. An adult son could have left home; this is neither proof nor disproof that Tennessee Robert was Archibald’s son. Robert’s father hypothesis remains possible, 51%; no mother or identity is assigned to an unnamed slot.<ref name="Newberry1810Original">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYBM-SHB United States census 1810, Newberry, page 119 A], NARA M 252 roll 61; FamilySearch index XH 2 Y-4 QW. Original linked image visually checked 30 October 2026.</ref>

The next useful test is Archibald’s 1818 estate 647, box 27, package 57: named heirs, distributions and receipts. No estate contents were read in this review.
